claims.evidence: No nameplate, VIN, or country-of-origin marking is legible in the photo; the green paint marks are just handling/export tags, not proof of sourcing.

risks.risk: Engine may not run or start (compression, internal wear, timing issues)
risks.proof: Video of the engine being started and running, showing exhaust and no unusual noise/smoke

risks.risk: Unknown make/model fitment, so buyer cannot confirm it matches the vehicle needing the part
risks.proof: Clear photo of an engine ID/VIN sticker or casting number stamped on the block
risks.if_unproven: price as generic unidentified engine, not model-specific

risks.risk: Missing or damaged internal components (pistons, timing chain, bearings) not visible externally
risks.proof: Video or photos of the engine with valve/timing cover removed, or a borescope clip

risks.risk: Incomplete accessories (turbo, ECU, sensors) despite wiring harness shown
risks.proof: Full 360° photo set showing all sides including turbo mount and ECU connector
risks.if_unproven: price as incomplete, missing standard accessories

risks.risk: Unknown mileage/hours and reason for removal (accident vs. failure)
risks.proof: Odometer photo from donor vehicle or dealer paperwork/invoice

risks.risk: Seller's claim of 'direct Korean parts' could be unverified sourcing used to inflate perceived value
risks.proof: Import documents, customs paperwork, or dealer certification showing origin
risks.if_unproven: price as generic used import, no premium for claimed origin

proof_requests: Video of the engine running (cold start, idle, revs)
Photo of engine ID plate, casting number, or VIN sticker
Photos showing all sides of the engine including turbo/ECU area
Any import or purchase documentation showing origin and history
response.reason: The witness confirms it is a used car engine, so it can be priced at worst case (unverified running condition, unknown fitment, unverifiable origin claim) pending the listed proofs.
